title: Global URL Shortener (TinyURL)
intro: Design a globally available URL shortener that converts long web URLs into compact 7-character aliases at 100:1 read-to-write scale.
objectives: Generate short keys using Base62 bijective encoding over 64-bit distributed IDs.
Evaluate 301 Permanent Redirect (browser caches, zero server load) vs 302 Temporary Redirect (analytics tracking).
Cache top 20% hot links in Redis to satisfy 99% of read requests sub-millisecond.
body:
### Capacity & Math
- **Write Traffic**: 100M URLs created/day $\approx 1,160$ write QPS.
- **Read Traffic**: 100:1 read-write ratio $\approx 116,000$ read QPS.
- **Key Space**: Using alphanumeric characters $[a-z, A-Z, 0-9]$ gives 62 symbols. A 7-character short URL supports:

$$62^7 \approx 3.52 \times 10^{12} \text{ (3.5 Trillion unique URLs)}$$

### Encoding Strategy
Avoid hashing (MD5/SHA256 truncated) as it produces hash collisions requiring expensive database existence lookups. Instead, use a **Distributed ID Generator** (Snowflake or counter range allocation) to obtain a globally unique 64-bit integer, and convert it directly to Base62 string representation.
keyIdea: Use a distributed unique ID generator combined with Base62 encoding to eliminate hash collisions completely. Offload 99% of reads using Redis and CDN edge caching.

concepts.title: 301 vs 302 Redirection
concepts.body: 301 redirects are cached permanently by browsers (bypassing your servers on subsequent clicks). 302 redirects force requests through your server every time, essential for click tracking and analytics.

concepts.title: Cache Eviction
concepts.body: Standard LRU cache retaining the most recently accessed links handles skewed virality distributions perfectly.

examples: bit.ly and t.co shortening billions of links.

quiz.prompt: Why is Base62 conversion of a distributed ID superior to truncating an MD5 hash?
options: Bijective Base62 conversion guarantees zero hash collisions
Base62 runs entirely in CPU cache
quiz.explanation: Converting a unique 64-bit integer to Base62 is a 1-to-1 mathematical mapping with 0% chance of collision.
